data.label: sg-alb (ALB): HTTP 80 from CloudFront prefix list only
Students & Librarians (Browser)
data.notes: Students and staff search, reserve and track books; librarians manage the catalogue and circulation desk. They open https://dxxxx.cloudfront.net (AWS Academy Learner Lab: no custom domain, so no Route 53 / ACM).

data.label: Amazon CloudFront (HTTPS *.cloudfront.net, edge cache for /assets/*)
data.notes: Viewer HTTPS with the default CloudFront certificate (Learner Lab has no custom domain). Redirect HTTP -> HTTPS. Default behaviour -> ALB, CachingDisabled + AllViewer. /assets/* -> CachingOptimized. Origin = Elastic Beanstalk domain, HTTP 80 inside AWS. Real account: Route 53 + ACM and an HTTPS origin.

data.label: AWS WAF web ACL (attached to CloudFront)
data.notes: Global web ACL on the CloudFront distribution (not a device in a subnet). Core rule set + SQL injection rules + rate-based rule + custom rule: block /api/internal/* without the x-internal-token header.

data.label: Internet Gateway (attached to the VPC)
data.notes: Attached to the VPC (drawn on the VPC border). Public route table 0.0.0.0/0 -> IGW.

data.label: NAT Gateway AZ-A (outbound only)
data.notes: Outbound internet for the private app subnets (EB agent, npm install, SES API). One NAT during build weeks to save cost.

data.label: Application Load Balancer (public, spans AZ-A + AZ-B)
data.notes: Created and managed by Elastic Beanstalk. HTTP :80 listener (users get HTTPS from CloudFront; no certificate without a domain in Learner Lab). Health check /api/health (checks the DB). Access logs -> S3 logs bucket. SG allows only the CloudFront origin-facing prefix list.

data.label: NAT Gateway AZ-B (scale-up: demo week)
data.notes: Second NAT added in demo week so each AZ has its own exit (removes the NAT single point of failure). Until then private-app-b routes through NAT-A.

data.label: VPC Interface Endpoints AZ-A (secretsmanager, sqs, logs, monitoring)
data.notes: Interface endpoints with private DNS: com.amazonaws.us-east-1.secretsmanager, .sqs, .logs, .monitoring. Keeps AWS API traffic inside the VPC. NAT is still needed for the EB agent and SES.

data.label: EC2 instance AZ-A (Elastic Beanstalk, Node.js 22 Express app)
data.notes: Node.js 22 on Amazon Linux 2023. Express API + React SPA. No public IP, no SSH key, IMDSv2 only. Instance profile LabInstanceProfile (Learner Lab).

data.label: Amazon ElastiCache (Valkey/Redis): catalogue cache
data.notes: Single cache.t4g.micro node, TLS in transit (rediss://). If it fails the app falls back to an in-memory cache, so it is not a hard dependency.

data.label: EC2 instance AZ-B (Elastic Beanstalk, Node.js 22 Express app)
data.notes: Second instance of the same Auto Scaling group, in AZ-B.

data.label: EC2 Auto Scaling group (min 2, max 4, CPU 70 %)
data.notes: Managed by Elastic Beanstalk. Min 2 / max 4 instances across both AZs; scale out at 70 % CPU, in at 25 %. Rolling with additional batch deployments.

data.label: VPC Interface Endpoints AZ-B (secretsmanager, sqs, logs, monitoring)
data.notes: Same four interface endpoints, ENIs in AZ-B.

data.label: Amazon RDS PostgreSQL 16 primary (AZ-A)
data.notes: db.t4g.micro, encrypted, not public. Master credentials managed in Secrets Manager. Reservations use BEGIN; SELECT ... FOR UPDATE; COMMIT so the last copy goes to exactly one student.

data.label: Amazon RDS standby (AZ-B, synchronous, automatic failover)
data.notes: Multi-AZ standby. Not readable; takes over automatically if the primary or AZ-A fails.

data.label: Amazon RDS read replica (AZ-B, async, read-only)
data.notes: Serves catalogue browsing queries (readQuery). Writes and reservations always go to the primary.

data.label: library-public-rt -> IGW
data.notes: Associated with public-a and public-b. 0.0.0.0/0 -> IGW.

data.label: library-private-rt -> NAT + S3 endpoint
data.notes: Associated with private-app-a/b. 0.0.0.0/0 -> NAT-A (NAT-B for app-b after scale-up); S3 prefix list -> S3 gateway endpoint. DB subnets have no internet route.

data.label: S3 Gateway Endpoint (free)
data.notes: Cover uploads from the instances reach S3 without the NAT Gateway.

data.label: Amazon S3: book covers (private, presigned URLs)
data.notes: Block all public access, SSE-S3. The app uploads covers and returns 1-hour presigned GET URLs; browsers download covers directly from S3.

data.label: Amazon S3: ALB access logs (Glacier after 30 days)
data.notes: Lifecycle: Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 30 days, expire after 365 days.

data.label: AWS Secrets Manager (RDS master credentials)
data.notes: RDS-managed secret (or a self-managed secret with host/dbname if the lab blocks the managed option). The app reads it at start-up through the interface endpoint.

data.label: Amazon SQS: library-notifications
data.notes: Standard queue, visibility timeout 180 s, redrive to the DLQ after 3 receives. The app publishes after COMMIT (transactional outbox).

data.label: AWS Lambda: library-notifier (outside the VPC)
data.notes: Node.js 22. SQS trigger, batch 10, ReportBatchItemFailures. Sends with SES, then reports sent/failed to the app (/api/internal/notifications/:id/status).

data.label: Amazon SES (verified sender)
data.notes: Verified sender identity. Sandbox: recipients verified; production access requested.

data.label: Amazon SQS: library-notifications-dlq
data.notes: Messages that failed 3 times. CloudWatch alarm when >= 1 message is visible.

data.label: Student inbox (email)
data.notes: Reservation confirmations, "now available", pickup / due / overdue reminders.

data.label: EventBridge Scheduler: library-daily (08:00 Asia/Thimphu)
data.notes: cron(0 8 * * ? *) in time zone Asia/Thimphu, 2 retries.

data.label: AWS Lambda: library-daily-reminders (outside the VPC)
data.notes: Calls POST /api/internal/jobs/daily (shared token): expires uncollected holds, promotes the waitlist, queues reminders. No DB credentials needed.

data.label: Amazon CloudWatch (logs, metrics, alarms, dashboard)
data.notes: EB instance logs (14 days), Lambda logs, dashboard cst-library. Alarms: unhealthy hosts, ALB 5xx, EC2 CPU, RDS CPU/storage, DLQ >= 1, Lambda errors.

data.label: Amazon SNS: library-alerts
data.notes: Email subscriptions for every team member.

data.label: AWS Elastic Beanstalk: cst-library-prod
data.notes: Manages the ALB, Auto Scaling group and EC2 instances. Enhanced health, managed platform updates, rolling with additional batch, auto rollback on failed health checks. Config in server/.ebextensions.

data.label: GitHub Actions (CI/CD: test, build, deploy)
data.notes: On push to main: test -> build -> package -> upload to S3 -> new EB version -> rolling deploy -> smoke test /api/health -> update both Lambdas. Learner Lab: signs in with the session keys stored as GitHub secrets (refreshed each session). Real account: OIDC role, no stored keys.

data.label: AWS IAM (LabRole / LabInstanceProfile)
data.notes: Learner Lab cannot create roles: LabRole is used by Elastic Beanstalk, both Lambdas and the scheduler, and LabInstanceProfile by the EC2 instances. Real-account design: library-ec2-role (one secret, one queue, covers/* only), separate Lambda roles, GitHub OIDC deploy role.
